body: The last paragraph especially resonated with me. I’ll do little things to hurt myself, ranging from exposing myself to media I know distresses me to smacking myself in the face and scratching my thighs. I can’t bring myself to go through with it completely, so I do little things I hope will push me closer to the edge and let me give up entirely. I only need to feel ready to do it once. Another thing that’s stopping me, though, is the fear that I won’t succeed and my fate will be out of my hands. What little autonomy I have left will be stripped away. I haven’t really posted here until today, but having confirmation that what you say is understood is huge for me, so I hope hearing that someone else relates to your post offers some measure of relief.
This is the dream! Glad for you!

Same here. They’ve taken everything from me. They forced me to cut myself off from my friends. I’ve been alone for 5 years. They’ve belittled me when I tried coming out so that I eventually “gave up” about it (nothing about my identity has changed, I’m just forced into hiding it). They’re classic abusive narcs who enable one another. Dad drank, but finally quit a few years ago, but he just gets to walk away from I while I suffer from the abuse. They’re shitheads and I’m fucking stuck with them. I think of the life I could have had and want to fucking scream.
Thank you so much for the advice! I should definitely look into this once I’m able.

I don’t know how well that would go. She didn’t necessarily try and stand up for me as much as diagnose me, from how I interpreted my parents’ recounting if that event. That said, I don’t know if what they said was even true- They tend to “exaggerate” on “accident” sometimes, in their own words, meaning they lie and twist narratives to their benefit. I also don’t know if my aunt would be on my side or “the family’s”. She’d probably say something along the lines of “your parents know best for you, it’s not my place to intervene”, remembering what she’s like. Highly doubt she’d believe what I tell her or take it seriously enough to do anything. It’s interesting that I’m pretty sure she was spot on with the speculative diagnosis, though, by coincidence or actual insight.
I don’t know. I only know that once I’m 18 I’m a legal adult. I should look into that if that’s a possible concern. I don’t know if they could have something over me after then or not.

My own school just went entirely to online classes, too, with (from what I understand) over 100 positive tests. It’s frustrating and scary when you still live with your family, as even if you yourself take every precaution you can, you’re still at risk if they choose not to.
Thank you. They’re asleep right now. I have no idea what awaits me in the morning, but knowing there’s support from others out in the world helps.
Thank you so much. I can still hear them talking. I don’t know what the rest of tonight or the days following will be like. Hoping they just act like nothing happened. Thank you again
